summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of idiopathic chronic pancreatitis was admitted for an acute flare characterized by persistent epigastric pain radiating to the back, nausea, and inability to tolerate oral intake. Despite normal lipase levels, her symptoms were consistent with prior episodes. She was managed with bowel rest, IV fluids, and IV hydromorphone for pain control. Her condition improved over three days, allowing transition to sips on hospital day two and clear liquids on day three. She was successfully switched back to her home oral pain and anti-nausea medications and tolerated oral intake without complications. Her chronic conditions, including depression, overactive bladder, GERD, and stable iron deficiency anemia, were maintained on baseline therapy. She was discharged home with instructions to slowly advance her diet, continue her medication regimen, and follow up with her GI specialist and primary care provider.
